verses.text: “Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘This is the thing which Yahweh has commanded,
Whatever man there is of the house of Israel, who kills a bull, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or who kills it outside the camp,

and hasn’t brought it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to offer it as an offering to Yahweh before Yahweh’s tabernacle: blood shall be imputed to that man. He has shed blood; and that man shall be cut off from among his people.

This is to the end that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices, which they sacrifice in the open field, that they may bring them to Yahweh, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them for sacrifices of peace offerings to Yahweh.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood on Yahweh’s altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and burn the fat for a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
They shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat idols, after which they play the prostitute. This shall be a statute forever to them throughout their generations.’
“You shall say to them, ‘Any man there is of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice,
and doesn’t bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, to sacrifice it to Yahweh; that man shall be cut off from his people.

“‘Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who eats any kind of blood, I will set my face against that soul who eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
Therefore I have said to the children of Israel, “No person among you may eat blood, nor may any stranger who lives as a foreigner among you eat blood.”

“‘Whatever man there is of the children of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who takes in hunting any animal or bird that may be eaten; he shall pour out its blood, and cover it with dust.

For as to the life of all flesh, its blood is with its life: therefore I said to the children of Israel, “You shall not eat the blood of any kind of flesh; for the life of all flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.”

“‘Every person that eats what dies of itself, or that which is torn by animals, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening: then he shall be clean.
But if he doesn’t wash them, or bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.’”

footnotes.content: The Lord opens His mouth again to Moses—not with judgment, but with a word that draws Israel closer to His altar. In every divine speech, I hear an invitation to know Him better. He speaks because He wants to be known.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses is told to gather Aaron, his sons, and all Israel to hear one word: this is what the Lord commands. There's such weight in that 'all'—no one left out, no rank that excuses them. The Lord's word binds the whole household together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Any man who kills a bull, lamb, or goat—whether in camp or out of it—without bringing it to the Tent of Meeting breaks covenant. The Lord claims authority over life itself; no slaughter is small, no killing is private from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blood shall be imputed to that man—he has shed it without the Lord's say. Being 'cut off' from the people meant losing your place, your name, your belonging. The Lord takes seriously the boundary between profane slaughter and holy sacrifice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The reason is plain: bring your sacrifices to the Tent, not into the open fields, so they may be offerings to Yahweh. The Lord does not hide Himself in secrecy; He draws His people to gather at His door, in light, where witness lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest sprinkles blood and burns fat—actions full of meaning. The Lord receives a pleasant aroma, and the ritual makes the invisible real. We learn by these gestures that our worship rises to heaven and is welcomed there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They shall no more sacrifice to goat idols after whom they prostitute themselves. The Lord will not share His altar with demons; He calls Israel away from the darkness of false worship into the clarity of truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the rule extends to foreigners living among Israel—any sojourner may bring an offering. The Lord's table makes room for the stranger; belonging is not by blood but by covenant obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whoever brings an offering but does not bring it to the Tent of Meeting shall be cut off. The location matters because it is where the Lord dwells, where heaven and earth touch. To bypass the sanctuary is to refuse the Lord's presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Any man who eats blood—I will set My face against that soul. The Lord's face turned toward you is mercy; His face set against you is the deepest aloneness. Blood-eating severs covenant because the blood belongs to the altar, not the belly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The life of the flesh is in the blood—I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement. Here the Lord reveals why blood matters: it carries life itself, and He uses it to cleanse us. Blood poured out on the altar speaks of sacrifice covering sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No person—Israelite or foreigner—may eat blood. The rule is universal because the truth beneath it is: life belongs to the Lord alone, and to consume blood is to usurp what He has claimed for Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When a hunter takes wild game, he must pour out its blood and cover it with dust. Even in the wilderness, far from the altar, the Lord's rule follows. To hunt is not to own; the blood goes back to Him, and the hunter kneels in respect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The life of all flesh is its blood—that truth appears again, underlined. No kind of flesh exempts you from this word. The Lord will not have His creatures' lives treated as mere meat; each one returns to Him through its blood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whoever eats what dies by itself or is torn by beasts must wash and bathe, and be unclean until evening. Even death that comes without ritual or intention brings separation; the Lord's holiness cannot be approached carelessly. But evening comes, and cleansing is possible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these old precepts: if we fail to wash, to turn back, to make ourselves right, we bear the weight of our own unfaithfulness. The Lord offers cleansing; we choose to accept it or carry it ourselves. As of 2026-10, His invitation remains open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
